absence_search_guard.leg_wide_limb: G23a ran over ALL 186 declared-unmatched rows in this run, with no exception list, and requires a non-empty `the_search_that_found_none` on each.
absence_search_guard.registry_limb_reach: G23b/c/d reach the rows carrying a `search_id`. The rows without one carry a PROSE search that was run and recorded but not registered in a re-runnable form; back-filling a registry entry for a search this run did not re-measure would be inventing the measurement, which is the defect the field exists to prevent. Stated as a bound, not papered over.
absence_search_guard.what_a_green_here_is_not: Evidence that any search was well-chosen. G23 checks that a search is NAMED, RUNNABLE and REACHED its population. Whether the population was the right one to look in, and whether the member's claim is really what the search looked for, are judgements — they are carried on the row in `why_this_search_is_this_claims_search` so a reader can disagree with them, and no refusal can reach them.

arithmetic.members_equation: population members = members with >=1 edge + members declared unmatched

axis_provenance.what_was_checked: every axis `expr`, every precondition `guard` and every listed conjunct occurs VERBATIM in the bytes at the span its row names — the emitting excerpt or a named context excerpt.

axis_span_provenance.what_this_does_not_establish: That a rejected row's span is the RIGHT one. It establishes that the row is not claiming the locator's authority for a span the locator did not give it. The bytes at the span are checked separately, and only when --harness is given.
axis_span_provenance.what_was_checked: For every `locator_row` row, the committed `emitting_byte_span` is one the locator names for that row's key. For every `locator_row_rejected` row, the locator's own `rung_pin_level` is NOT `row`, the span used is NOT one the locator names, and a reason is recorded. An unknown provenance value is refused.

cells.note:
THE FIRST ET CLAIM IN THE CROSSWALK TO CONTRADICT `WireSchemaValid`, and three things about it have to be said or it will be misread.
(1) WHY THE CHECK IS GREEN AT THE ACCEPTED RUN. The harness ran against `conformance/server_handler.ex`, which sends a MAP — the file says so itself: ``MRTR.input_required/2` is spec'd `list() | nil` while the wire type `InputRequests` is a JSON object keyed by input name. This file sends a map, per the schema.` So the conformance adapter and this unit disagree with EACH OTHER about the SDK's own wire shape, and the accepted run only ever saw the adapter.
(2) WHY IT IS THE SDK'S PROPERTY AND NOT THE FIXTURE'S. `MCP.Protocol.Messages.MRTR.input_required/2` is `@spec input_required(list() | nil, binary() | nil)` and puts the value through untouched. The list is what the SDK's own type says to pass; a handler that follows the spec is contradicting the spec of the function it calls.
(3) WHICH OF THE FOURTEEN `WireSchemaValid` ROWS. The contradiction holds against ALL FOURTEEN of the family's `WireSchemaValid` rows, because all fourteen are one generic validator and the offending message would be the same in every scenario. ONE edge is filed, against the `input-required-result-request-state` row, because that is the scenario whose flow this unit mirrors — a `requestState` round trip. Fourteen edges would be one finding counted fourteen times and would inflate every figure this file reports; recording the scope here is the alternative to both.
oc_key: Every JSON-RPC message the implementation sent is valid per the spec JSON schema for the negotiated spec version

cells.claim: a TextContent encodes to the wire with the discriminator `text` synthesised by the encoder, and with its text carried
cells.evidence: content_test.exs:42 — `decoded["type"] == "text"` — and content_test.exs:43 — `decoded["text"] == "test"`. citation_verbatim_guard.reach: `quotes_compared` equals `quotes_counted`, and that attests exactly one thing: NO QUOTE FAILED TO PLACE. It is NOT an independent recount, and by itself it is not evidence of reach. Both figures come out of ONE traversal in `audit/3` — `quotes_counted` is the length of the quote list that traversal built and `quotes_compared` counts the members of that same list which matched — so the equality is another spelling of `no quote-level defect`, and a sweep that read NOTHING satisfies it at 0 == 0, as does one reading a field that does not exist. What bears on reach here is the MAGNITUDE and never the equality: `quotes_compared` quotes placed, over `records_with_evidence` records, over `records_visited` visited. The independent recount — the span regex walked a SECOND time over the same records by code that is not `audit/3` — and the `counted > 0` that stops an empty population passing both live in `conformance/controls/citation_verbatim_controls.exs`, not in this artefact. The record population is every top-level list of objects in each edges file, so a collection a later ticket adds is inside the guard without being named here.
citation_verbatim_guard.what_it_does_not_establish: That a quote SUPPORTS the verdict it is filed under — that is a judgement and A3 §7's residual, and no refusal reaches it. That a backticked PROSE phrase is accurate: only source-shaped spans are compared, so an inaccurate paraphrase in backticks passes, and the ruling's remedy is to de-quote prose rather than to widen the shape test until English fails it. That a quoted byte-string in a field OTHER than `evidence` is verbatim — the gap between `records_visited` and `records_with_evidence` is exactly that population, reported rather than implied.
citation_verbatim_guard.what_was_checked: Every SOURCE-SHAPED backtick span in `evidence` — one carrying `=`, `(`, `[`, `!==` or `===` — occurs VERBATIM and CONTIGUOUS, modulo runs of whitespace, inside a window the evidence itself ADDRESSES: the cited `file.exs:N[-M]` span in the repo, or a byte span the axis row for this edge's tag names in the harness build. Two limbs: WINDOWING (the comparison is against the cited span, never the whole artefact) catches a right-bytes/wrong-line citation; CONTIGUITY (one squashed string, substring containment) catches a quote spliced from lines that are real and non-adjacent. A bare `:N` continuation is refused as a FORM — it has no syntactic referent and resolving it by proximity is guessing. An elision inside a source-shaped span is refused rather than fragment-matched, because matching `A … B`'s halves green-lights a quote whose parts sit arbitrarily far apart, which is the composed-quote hole this guard exists to close.

Chosen because the residual is a WHOLE CLAIM of the member rather than a sharper reading of a claim that already has an edge: `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `public` are edges, and `and these are the DEFAULTS` is a third thing the member asserts and nothing scores. The file still has no criterion that would make this choice forced rather than argued — see the note on the `:237/:238` edge, and MES-110.
rows.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `DefaultResultTypeComplete` — and it is the only row in all 175 that matches `(?i)\bdefault|\bconfigur`, so a reader greping for `default` finds exactly one hit and could stop at it. It is not a counterpart on three counts: it is CLIENT leg, its subject is `resultType` rather than any caching field, and its `default` is a SPEC default — how a client must read an ABSENT field — not a deployment's unconfigured state. The nearer rows by subject are this file's own five `*CachingHints` plus `TtlNonNegative` and `CacheScopeValid`, which this member DOES carry edges onto; they score the values and are silent on where the values came from.
rows.the_search_that_found_none: an OC check that establishes what a server does when a policy is NOT configured — a DEFAULT as distinct from a setting — by varying the implementation's configuration between runs or by reading it, rather than scoring whatever values the single server under test happened to return
rows.why_it_is_recorded_here_and_not_in_bucke: The member is EDGE-BEARING — its two value assertions carry four edges between them — and a bucket-1 row is a statement about a MEMBER with no counterpart at all. A3 §6's state 3 is a property of a member, so a sub-claim of an edge-bearing member has no bucket and is escalated instead. The placement among the three the file uses for such residuals is argued in `placement_and_why`.
rows.why_no_axis_reaches_it: Every caching axis is a predicate on a result the harness received from ONE server in ONE configuration; nothing in the suite varies a server's configuration or asks what it was, so no OC check can distinguish a value that was configured from one that was not. The distinction is the whole point of this member — it is the regression guard on the no-store default — and it is invisible to the harness in principle rather than by omission.

claim_level_unmatched.what_this_is: A claim within an EDGE-BEARING member that has no counterpart in its file's declared check population. A3 §6's state 3 is a property of a member, so there is no bucket for this and none is invented.

cross_source_agreement.what_this_is: A CONSISTENCY pin, not a correctness one (ruling 9). Both artefacts descend from the same accepted harness run: agreement witnesses that nobody edited one without regenerating the other, and a wrong run would be wrong in both.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `sep-2243-x-mcp-header-primitive-only` / `ClientRejectsInvalidTool_invalid_object_header` — `Client MUST NOT call tool 'invalid_object_header' with invalid x-mcp-header`. The word `object` is right there in a CG7 check, and it is not this case. Its fixture is `data:{type:`object`,"x-mcp-header":`Data`}`: an annotation whose OWN property is object-typed, which is invalid because only primitives may be mirrored. The claim here is the opposite and legitimate case — an annotation on a STRING property that sits inside another object's `properties` — and the reachability question (is every step of the chain a `properties` key?) is never put: the measurement above finds zero `properties:` nested inside a `properties:` anywhere in the two CG7 scenarios' 14027 bytes, while 14 `properties:{` and 55 `x-mcp-header` occurrences show the sweep reading the right bytes. Every annotation in the CG7 fixture sits one step down.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `sep-2243-client-encode-values` / `ClientCustomHeader_Priority` — `Client sends correct Mcp-Param-Priority header (INTEGER value)`. The suite does score an integer header value, on the client leg, in CG7, and this file already carries an edge to it. The value it scores is `42`. The safe-range boundary is 9007199254740991, sixteen digits; the search finds zero integer literals of sixteen digits or more in the two CG7 scenarios, and the largest integer anywhere in them is the 42 the positive control returns. So the constraint exists in the spec and in our implementation, the suite has a check in the right place, and its fixture never reaches the boundary.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `sep-2322-default-result-type-complete` / DefaultResultTypeComplete, decomposed by this ticket. It is the ONE case in this fixture where the client MUST NOT retry — so it looks like the counterpart, and the resemblance survives a careless read. Its antecedent is different: the failing arm is `if(t)` where `t` is `Client retried with inputResponses even though the result had no resultType`. The trigger is an ABSENT `resultType`, which the spec says defaults to `complete`; this claim's trigger is a resultType that explicitly SAYS `input_required` while the client has nothing configured to resolve it. And the fixture rules the declining client out from the other side: the scenario's `getChecks` seeds every unfired MRTR check `status:`FAILURE`` with `Tool was not called by client or MRTR flow not completed`, so a client that declines is scored as having failed the flow, never as having correctly declined. Both of the fixture's two `input_required` emissions ([345526] and [346965], measured) lead into a retry the checks then score.

It is the suite's only row about a server producing an error at all, and a reader could take it for this. It is not: its subject is a TOOL returning a declared error result through the protocol's own error channel, which is the server working correctly. This claim's subject is the server's own INFRASTRUCTURE failing — a collector that will not start, an identity factory that raises, a chunked response that cannot open — where there is no tool-level error to return and the only question is what the client is told instead.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `ServerSSEStreamsFunctional` — `Multiple POST SSE streams should be functional` — and it is a near miss a reader is very likely to stop at, because the harness genuinely pipes each stream through an SSE PARSER before reading it. It is still not a counterpart, and the decomposition of that check is what settles it: the stream is scored by racing ONE `read()` against a 2 second timer, and a `null` from the timer is not recorded as an error, so a stream whose frames are malformed enough to yield nothing is counted FUNCTIONAL exactly as one that delivers a frame. The event is never decoded and its payload is never compared with the request that opened it. So the check cannot distinguish correct framing from no framing at all, and nothing else in the 175 mentions an SSE field line. The second near miss is `SRV13`'s territory — the SSE response HEADERS — which is a different absence with its own entry and is named here only so the two are not confused.
declared_unmatched.the_search_that_found_none: the SYNTAX of an SSE frame — the `event:`, `id:`, `data:` and `retry:` field lines, the blank line that terminates a frame, and the folding of a multi-line payload into one `data:` line per line
declared_unmatched.why_no_counterpart: `no-oc-scenario` — the suite carries SSE rows and not one of them reads a frame. MEASURED over all 175: zero mention any SSE field line, and the two rows that do open streams count a stream that yields nothing as functional.
declared_unmatched.why_this_search_is_this_claims_search: The claim is about the BYTES of an SSE frame. SRV30's subject is that syntax, and its near miss is the reason a narrower instrument would mislead: the suite does carry SSE rows, they do run a parser, and they still cannot see framing — so a search that stopped at `is there an SSE check` would answer yes and be wrong about this claim.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `CacheScopeValid` — `All cacheScope values are "public" or "private"` — and this is the sharpest near miss in the file, because the two are about the SAME configuration and reach OPPOSITE conclusions about it without contradicting each other. A `cacheScope` of `public` on an identity-dependent response is exactly what this member warns about, and it is exactly what `CacheScopeValid` PASSES: the check's axis is an enumeration over two string literals and has no notion of who the response was built for. So the OC scores the value's VALIDITY and the member scores the deployment's SAFETY, and a server can be green on the first while being the thing the second exists to catch. The general reason for the zero is `SRV27`'s and is not restated: the harness scores messages, and a warning crosses no wire. What is new here is that the diagnostic fires at `Plug.init/1` — once per configuration, never per request — so there is no request for a harness to attach it to even in principle.

keying_control.measure: ROWS LOST — rows that disappear when the projection is deduplicated. A1's measure and match-relation.md §5's, so the keyings are compared in the unit those documents already use.
keying_control.the_row_this_leg_DEPENDS_on: `sep-2243-client-includes-standard-headers` — NINE in-denominator client checks share that one `check_id`: ClientMcpMethodHeader_tools_list / _tools_call / _resources_list / _resources_read / _prompts_list / _prompts_get and ClientMcpNameHeader_tools_call / _resources_read / _prompts_get, plus the 2 SKIPPED ones, 11 rows on one id. Keying on `check_id` would merge nine CLIENT checks into one; A1's six-field key merges none. It is CG1's whole scenario, so it is a row the client leg depends on rather than an example quoted from A1 — and it is why the control stays on the 173: re-scoped to CG7's 29, the `name` and `description` limbs lose NOTHING (measured 0 of 54 on the whole client leg) and could not fire at all, which is the vacuity the two-direction design exists to prevent.
keying_control.what_the_crosswalk_is_keyed_on: A3's token for the address and A1's six-field key for the join. The token carries five fields; `description` cannot live in a test name, so reversibility is THROUGH A1's manifest, not lexical.
keying_control.what_the_two_directions_establish: POSITIVE: the obvious keyings DO merge rows on this population, so the hazard is real here and not merely quoted from A1. NEGATIVE: A1's six-field key merges none. Either direction alone is vacuous — a control that only ran the second would pass over a crosswalk keyed on `id`.

checks_addressed_outside_the_declared_ch.what_this_is: Checks an edge addresses that no file declares. They carry adjudicated edges and take NO part in bucket 2, because bucket 2 is a complement and these checks are not in any declared universe to be complemented within.
checks_addressed_outside_the_declared_ch.why_this_is_not_refused: An edge addresses the check its claim is about; refusing one outside the declared check population would force a file to declare every scenario it touches, and then bucket 2 would report every UNADJUDICATED sibling as having no ET counterpart. That is the false claim the third state exists to prevent.

check_population.rule: EVERY in-denominator OC check on the CLIENT leg — all 54, across all seven of its scenarios. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed, and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.denotes: All 54 in-denominator CLIENT checks — `http-custom-headers` 18 + `http-invalid-tool-headers` 11 (CG7) + `http-standard-headers` 9 (CG1) + `json-schema-ref-no-deref` 1 (CG4) + `request-metadata` 8 + `sep-2322-client-request-state` 5 + `tools_call` 2 (C1b-iii). Those seven scenarios ARE the client leg in the locator's artefact, so with C1b-iii's three added the declared check population and the client leg's in-denominator checks are the same set. The selector names the SCENARIOS rather than the 54 tokens, so a check added to any of them by a harness bump joins the population instead of falling silently outside it.
selector.evaluated: 54 checks denoted; equal to the count this file declares, and every one of them is axis-decomposed (G19).
selector.source_owner: MES-97 (C1a) — `mix conformance.locator`'s output, one row per in-denominator check
selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and the reason bucket 2 can now be non-empty. C1a derived its check population from the tags its own edges carried, so bucket 2 — the complement of the edge-bearing checks within it — was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` was a vacuous truth. Declaring the checks from outside the file is what makes the question answerable.
selector.why_the_locator_artefact_and_not_A1s_man: A1's manifest nests its checks under scenarios and its key is a six-field LIST; the selector's `key_field` must name a string field, and refuses anything else rather than stringifying it. The locator artefact is flat, carries one row per in-denominator check, and already carries the TOKEN — which is the field the edges in this file address checks by, so the two sides are compared in the same unit.

leg_totality.and_what_it_does_not: That any adjudication is RIGHT. It is a totality guard, not a correctness one: a leg every member of which was adjudicated wrongly passes it exactly as firmly. The state-4 guard over this population is still ENTAILED by G15a and still cannot fire (residual X7) — what G22b adds is that the population it cannot fire over is now provably the WHOLE leg rather than a slice somebody chose, and that scope claim is not entailed by anything.

files.rule: Every ET-CC member B2b attributes to the CLIENT leg. The leg is reached as the UNION of the four ticket slices that adjudicated it — CG7 (C1b-i), CG1/CG2/CG4 (C1b-ii), NO CG AT ALL (C1b-iii), and whatever C1a had already tagged — and the union is now the whole leg: every client row in B2b carries a `cg` in {CG7, CG1, CG2, CG4} or carries none, so the four limbs are exhaustive over it. NOTHING outside the client leg is adjudicated here.

selector.denotes: 107 ET-CC members — the WHOLE client leg. C1b-i declared 45 (CG7's 29 plus C1a's 18 moved rows, overlapping in 2). C1b-ii added 20 new homes from its 23 CG1/CG2/CG4 rows — three CG2 rows already sat inside the 45 through the `tokens` limb and were not re-homed — taking it to 65. C1b-iii's sub-population, `leg = client AND cg is_null`, is 55 rows and adds 42 new homes, not 55: THIRTEEN of the 55 carry C1a `oc:` tokens and so were already inside through the same `tokens` limb. 65 + 42 = 107. The one-home rule is preserved exactly by not re-homing those thirteen, which is the shape C1b-ii recorded for its three.
selector.evaluated: 107 members denoted; set-equal to the population this file derives in both directions (G15a). The counts block was checked field by field (G15b).
selector.is_null_is_not_get_equals_nil: The `cg is_null` limb is `has_key?(row, "cg") and get(row, "cg") == nil`. Under the weaker `get(row,"cg") == nil` an ABSENT field and a null one are the same thing, so a B2b schema change dropping `cg` would make the limb denote EVERY row and silently re-declare this population as all 281 — reconciling perfectly over a universe nobody chose. As implemented an absent field denotes NOTHING, the denotation collapses, and G15a reds naming every member as `extra`. Measured at this tip: all 281 rows carry the key, so the two readings are indistinguishable on live data and only a unit separates them. Both limbs are unit-tested and the absent-field case is shown separately (`crosswalk_controls.exs selectors`).
selector.what_this_is: The EXECUTABLE half of `rule`. The generator evaluates it against the source named below and requires the result to be SET-EQUAL, in both directions, to the population this file derives. Prose only becomes a guard when something can run it.
selector.why_it_must_name_a_file_other_than_this_: C1a derived its declared population by unioning the register_keys the edges file itself carried, so a dropped row did not violate the universe, it SHRANK it — measured on MES-99, both a dropped edge and a dropped declared_unmatched row built cleanly at 20 members with every set comparison still exact. A selector that read this file's own rows would be circular by another route.
selector.why_the_cg_conjunct_and_not_the_whole_cl: HISTORY, kept because the selector's SHAPE is a consequence of it. MES-104 was re-scoped to C1b-i = CG7 at the plan hop, so the leg arrived in three instalments — C1b-i CG7, C1b-ii CG1+CG2+CG4, C1b-iii the members with no CG — and the selector is the union of those slices. The union now covers the leg, and it is NOT collapsed into `leg equals client` for the reason recorded in `why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_slices_and_not_`leg_equals_client``.
selector.why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_sli: The four limbs now denote the whole leg, so `leg equals client` alone would denote the same 107 today — and it is NOT used, deliberately. G22b evaluates `all_of[{leg equals client}]` FRESH against B2b and set-compares it with this file's members. Under a bare-leg top-level selector that comparison would be ENTAILED by G15a's and could never fire: the X7 shape, a guard as empty as one nobody calls. Under the union shape the two ask different questions, and one mutation separates them — add a B2b row with `leg=client, cg="CG9"` and G15a stays green at 107 against 107 while G22b goes red at 108 against 107. That mutation is committed (`crosswalk_controls.exs totality`) and runs in the same run as the unmutated build.

check_population.rule: EVERY in-denominator OC check on the SERVER LEG — all 119 of them, across THIRTY-SEVEN scenarios, which is every server scenario the suite has. `server-stateless` 30 (C1c-i's), the FOURTEEN `input-required-result-*` scenarios 36 between them (C1c-ii's), the NINETEEN feature-endpoint scenarios 41 between them (C1c-iii's, declared there and reached by C1c-iii-b's members), and C1c-iv's THREE transport/security misc scenarios — `caching` 8, `dns-rebinding-protection` 2 and `server-sse-multiple-streams` 2 — 12 between them. 30 + 36 + 41 + 12 = 119. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed (12 by A3, 18 by C1c-i, 36 by C1c-ii, 41 by C1c-iii, 12 by C1c-iv), and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.denotes: All 119 in-denominator checks of the thirty-seven scenarios named — which, MEASURED against the locator artefact at this tip, is the WHOLE server leg: the locator carries 119 server rows and this selector denotes all 119, in both directions. `server-stateless` 30, the fourteen `input-required-result-*` scenarios 36, the nineteen feature-endpoint scenarios 41, and the three misc scenarios 12. THIRTY-SEVEN clauses, where C1c-i had one, C1c-ii fifteen and C1c-iii thirty-four, and every one is an equality rather than a prefix — see `why_fourteen_clauses_and_not_a_prefix`, whose reasoning C1c-iv applies unchanged to `caching`, `dns-rebinding-protection` and `server-sse-multiple-streams`.
selector.evaluated: 119 checks denoted; equal to the count this file declares, and every one of them is axis-decomposed (G19).
selector.source_owner: MES-97 (C1a) — `mix conformance.locator`'s output, one row per in-denominator check
selector.the_bound_this_leaves: THERE IS NO LONGER A SCENARIO BOUND, and that is a change of kind rather than of size. Until C1c-iv-a the declared CHECK population was a PROPER subset of the server leg, so a bucket-1 row meant `no counterpart among these N` and not `no counterpart on our leg`, and FOUR rows were scoped that way and said so in their `kind`: SRV02 and SRV18 named REAL counterparts in `dns-rebinding-protection`, SRV07 and SRV20 in `caching`, each so that whichever later C1c slice declared those scenarios would inherit the member rather than re-search for it. THIS IS THAT SLICE. (C1c-iv-a) All four members now carry edges onto the checks their own near misses named, all four registry entries are GONE, and the kind `no-oc-check-in-this-scenario` no longer occurs anywhere in this file — there is no undeclared server scenario left for it to mean anything about. C1c-i's SRV08 was the first of the five and C1c-ii discharged it; these four are the last. What remains is the LEG bound, which is a different thing and is unchanged: a `no-oc-server-check` row still means `none on OUR leg`, and it names the client-leg counterparts it is not denying.
selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and what makes bucket 2 answerable. It names the SCENARIO rather than the 119 tokens, so a check added to it by a harness bump joins the population instead of falling silently outside it.
selector.why_fourteen_clauses_and_not_a_prefix: A prefix clause would be SHORTER and would declare a DIFFERENT population: every future scenario whose name begins `input-required-result-` would join this file's declared checks the moment a harness bump introduced it, and would then have to be axis-decomposed by G19 or redden a build nobody had changed. Enumerating costs fourteen lines and makes the population a decision this ticket took rather than a pattern that keeps deciding. The same reasoning is why the client file enumerates its seven.
selector.why_the_feature_endpoint_scenarios_are_e: (C1c-iii) NINETEEN more equality clauses and not three `starts_with` ones. A prefix over `tools-` would be three lines instead of eight and would declare a DIFFERENT population: every future scenario a harness bump named `tools-call-something` would join this file's declared checks the moment it appeared, and would then have to be axis-decomposed by G19 or redden a build nobody had changed. The cost is real and is paid knowingly — the prefix would also have silently ADMITTED `tools-call-with-logging`, `tools-call-sampling` and `tools-call-elicitation`, three scenarios that exist in this very build and are NOT in C1c-iii's 41. That is not a hypothetical about a future bump; it is a live mis-declaration the prefix form would have made today.
selector.why_the_locator_artefact_and_not_A1s_man: A1's manifest nests its checks under scenarios and its key is a six-field LIST; the selector's `key_field` must name a STRING field and refuses anything else rather than stringifying it. The locator artefact is flat and carries a `token`. Same reason the client file gives.
selector.why_the_three_misc_scenarios_are_enumera: (C1c-iv-a) THREE more equality clauses and not a `starts_with` or a bare `leg equals server`. The bare-leg form is the tempting one now that the denotation IS the leg, and it is refused for the reason the client file gives on the member side, in its selector's note on why it is still a union of slices and not a bare leg test: the enumeration and the leg are two different questions that happen to have the same answer today, and collapsing them would make the check population a pattern that keeps deciding rather than a decision this file's tickets took. It also has a live cost. A harness bump adding a thirty-eighth server scenario would join this population silently under the bare-leg form and would then have to be axis-decomposed by G19 or redden a build nobody had changed; under the enumeration it falls outside, and the file says so. The same reasoning that rejected a `tools-` prefix at C1c-iii, applied to the case where the prefix would be the empty string.

leg_totality.and_what_it_does_not: That any adjudication is RIGHT. It is a totality guard, not a correctness one: a leg every member of which was adjudicated wrongly passes it exactly as firmly. The state-4 guard over this population is still ENTAILED by G15a and still cannot fire (residual X7) — what G22b adds is that the population it cannot fire over is now provably the WHOLE leg rather than a slice somebody chose, and that scope claim is not entailed by anything.

selector.what_the_two_conjuncts_are_for_and_why_N:
THE SHAPE IS PM-RATIFIED ON THIS TICKET'S PLAN HOP (Q1, option ii, 2026-09-24) AND THE ALTERNATIVE WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS REJECTED. Q2 ratified dropping C1a's first conjunct — the `tokens non_empty OR contradicts_oc not_null` limb, which denoted 1 of these 29. Taken literally that leaves a bare `none_of[client, server]`, and a bare `none_of` makes G22b ENTAILED and unable to fire: G22b evaluates a fresh `all_of[{leg equals none_determinable}]` and compares it by set, so under the bare form its denotation is a SUBSET of this selector's for every input, and it can differ from the file's members only where G15a has already failed. That is the X7 shape — a guard as empty as one nobody calls — and there is NO mutation that reds G22b with G15a green.

So the module conjunct is added, which is the conjunct both leg-scoped files already carry, and the separating mutation then EXISTS: a B2b row with `leg: none_determinable` in a TENTH module is denoted by no `starts_with` leaf, so G15a compares 29 denoted against 29 rows and PASSES while G22b compares 30 against 29 and REFUSES, naming it. That mutation is committed and runs beside the unmutated build (`crosswalk_controls.exs totality`).

AND THE LEG CONJUNCT IS LOAD-BEARING HERE IN A WAY IT IS ON NEITHER OTHER FILE — measured, not argued. SIX of the 9 modules also hold rows on another leg: `MCP.Protocol.CapabilitiesTest` 6 client / 2 server, `MCP.Protocol.HeaderMirrorTest` 17 / 1, `MCP.ProtocolTest` 5 / 2, `MCP.Transport.SSETest` 10 / 8, `MCP.Transport.SelfCompatibilityTest` 0 / 4, `MCP.Transport.SubscriptionsStreamTest` 0 / 17. Only three of the 9 modules are none_determinable throughout: `MCP.IntegrationTest`, `MCP.Protocol.ExtensionsTest` and `MCP.Transport.StdioTest`.

selector.why_none_of_and_not_an_enumeration_of_th:
`leg` happens to take three values in B2b today, so `any_of[{leg equals none_determinable}]` would denote the same 29 rows. It would do so only while that remains true: a fourth leg value would silently pull its members INTO this population — or, under the enumeration form, silently drop them — and nothing would go red. `none_of[client, server]` states the rule the prose states, which is `what neither adjudicated leg has taken`, and carries no assumption about the field's range. MES-105 added the `server` limb for exactly the reason MES-104 wrote the clause this way: the selector had to change when a leg was taken, and changing one leaf is the whole change.

IT ALSO KEEPS THIS FILE'S SELECTOR AND G22b'S APART, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES G22b ABLE TO FIRE. G22b's fresh selector is the enumeration form — `leg equals none_determinable` — and this one is the complement form. Writing both as the enumeration would make them the same question in the same words.

Every ET-CC member B2b puts on the client leg carries a row here — all 107 of them — and a member in neither an edge nor a declared_unmatched record REFUSES THE BUILD (G22b), evaluated fresh against B2b and compared by set in both directions. The leg was reached by 4 ticket slices declared as a COVER and not a partition: 18 members sit in two slices at once, because a member a later ticket's CG brings in may already have carried an earlier ticket's token, and it keeps ONE home. The overlap is derived here, not taken from the file's word for it, so the slices cannot be summed into a leg that is not one. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a claim that any adjudication is right. A leg every member of which was adjudicated wrongly passes G22b exactly as firmly, and the state-4 guard over this population remains ENTAILED by G15a and unable to fire (X7) — what is new is that the population it cannot fire over is provably the whole leg rather than a slice somebody chose.

Axis verdicts are JUDGEMENTS. Whether a claim really agrees with a conjunct is A3 §7's semantic-sameness residual and escalates per case; nothing here decides it.

FALSIFICATION-TESTED by C3 (MES-99) and STANDING — the attempts were made and none succeeded, which is not the same as proven. The bound is narrow. The generator now refuses a duplicated join key (G14), a population that is not the set its external selector denotes or that disagrees with its own declared counts (G15), and a manifest whose verdicts have drifted from A5's bucket-0 artefact (G16). Every falsification class is shown firing on a mutated input with the unmutated build as the negative control in the same run, at the OS exit status and not only in-VM, and restored green after; C1a's own thirteen are re-run with the after-restoration they lacked. A per-row bucket-assignment drift is caught naming the row and the buckets it crosses (conformance/controls/crosswalk_falsification_controls.exs). What that does NOT establish: that any axis verdict is right (X1 is untouched — an axis verdict is a judgement and no refusal can reach it), and that anything outside the declared population was falsified at all. MES-104 added four refusals to the set C3 covers — G17 (two files declaring the same member), G18 (an axis row citing a provenance for its emitting span the locator does not support), G19 (a DECLARED check with no axis decomposition) and G20 (an inherited B2b token no row carries) — each shown firing on a mutated input with the unmutated build as the negative control in the same run. MES-108 added G21, which refuses a population figure in this generator's own prose that the run did not derive. What lies OUTSIDE the declared population is unfalsified, and the tickets that own it are the ones `population.outside_the_population.owners` names — this residual does not name them, because it named C1b-ii while C1b-ii was rendering it, and a statement that names its own producer as still owing the remainder is CR-1 (MES-104) recurring as CR-5 (MES-108).

The second-source re-derivation (`--verdicts-from bucket-0`) is a CONSISTENCY pin, not a correctness one (ruling 9). A1's manifest and A5's bucket-0 artefact are different files, different schemas, different generators — but both descend from the SAME accepted harness run. Byte-identical output witnesses that nobody edited one without regenerating the other. A wrong run would be wrong in both, and this pin would agree just as firmly.
Axis spans address ONE build. A harness bump invalidates them, and --harness is what detects it — a run without it records `harness_checked: false` rather than a pass.

`no_axis_contact` is a THIRD escalation, added here by generalising A3 §2's 'covering zero of one axis is no match, not a partial one' to N axes. A3 §3's table has no row for it. Escalation rather than a new bucket is deliberate: it routes to the PM and costs nothing if the ruling goes the other way.

The member population is 281 across 3 edges files — 107 members from crosswalk-edges-client.json and 145 members from crosswalk-edges-server.json and 29 members from crosswalk-edges.json. Two of the checks C1a addresses enter through A3 §1's cardinality rule and §4's published worked edge, not through B2b's tokens — inherited, not newly adjudicated, and said so in the edges file. Every figure in this sentence is interpolated: all three were literals until MES-108, and two of the three were already wrong when CR-5 found them.

A3 §6's STATE-4 GUARD IS ENTAILED BY G15a and cannot fire. The population is set-equal to its selector's denotation in both directions and is derived from the file's own rows, so every member has a row and every row has a tag. This was already true in C1a, where the selector and the tagging predicate were literally the same predicate — so D3's claim that the state-4 guard 'is the limb that makes an EMPTY crosswalk fail' is not what happens: `check_population([], tagged)` returns `:ok`, and the vacuum guard is what fires. Recorded rather than removed, because the guard is A3 §6's ratified one and dropping it would be a silent change to a ratified rule. The completeness question that is NOT entailed is G20.

BUCKET 2 WAS EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION UNTIL MES-104. C1a derived its check universe from the tags its own edges carried, so the complement within it was necessarily empty and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` could not have said anything else. A file may now declare its check population from an external anchor. This run's answer is 91 of the 173 declared checks carrying no edge from any ET-CC member. A file that declares none contributes none to the universe and the artefact reports that bucket 2 was not asked, rather than reporting a zero. The answer is interpolated — this sentence froze C1b-i's at nine and went on stating it after MES-108 moved the check population (CR-5).

A CLAIM-LEVEL STATE 3 HAS NO BUCKET. A3 §6's state 3 is a property of a MEMBER, and the bucket-1 reconciliation requires a member to be edge-bearing or declared unmatched, never both — so a member matching on some claims and not on others has nowhere to record the unmatched ones. C1b-i found five; MES-108 resolved two of them into real edges and found one more. This run carries 7 of them in `claim_level_unmatched`, each with the search that found none, and ESCALATED — the figure interpolated, because it was written as a word and so would not have moved (CR-5). Whether A3 §6 should gain a claim-level state is the PM's.

THE ABSENCE-SEARCH REGISTRY DOES NOT REACH EVERY BUCKET-1 ROW, and the shortfall is stated rather than hidden behind a green. G23's prose limb is LEG-WIDE with no exception list — every declared-unmatched row in this run records the search that found none, and the two rows that did not when MES-109 opened were fixed by RUNNING their searches, not by excepting them. Its registry limb — id resolves, entry records a zero over a named population with a runnable pattern, positive controls and a near miss, no orphans, and the entry's kind equal to the row's own reason slug — reaches only the rows that carry a `search_id`. The rest carry a search that was run and recorded in prose but never registered, and registering it now would mean writing a zero this run did not re-measure: the invented-field defect C1b-i refused when it declined to backfill. C1c faces the same choice on the server leg and should settle it there rather than inherit it silently.

every_declared_check_is_decomposed_and_a.equation: declared checks = checks with an edge + bucket 2
every_declared_check_is_decomposed_and_a.why_this_is_not_a_set_equality: C1a asserted `every declared check appears` as a set equality, and it held TRIVIALLY: the declared set was derived from the tags the edges carried, so the two sides were the same list twice. Once the checks are declared from outside the file the equality is no longer expected — the checks that do NOT appear are bucket 2, which is the answer rather than a failure.

totality.measure: SET COMPARISON, not arithmetic — two counts agreeing is not two sets agreeing.
totality.negatives_are_enumerated_not_counted: Bucket 1's members and bucket 2's checks are listed by name in `buckets`, and the not_yet_adjudicated remainder is counted with its owner named (A2d / ruling 4).

trust_status: FALSIFICATION-TESTED by C3 (MES-99) and STANDING — over the declared 281-member / 173-declared-check slice and no further. Both figures are INTERPOLATED from the population this run derives, and the slice is NOT decomposed by ticket here. The pair was a literal that had to be re-typed by hand at every move of the population: it was re-typed at MES-104, the population moved again at MES-108, and it was not. That is an argument against the SHAPE and not against an author — it is CR-1 (MES-104) recurring in the one generator CR-1's remedy did not reach (CR-5, MES-108). The parenthetical was the worse half — it enumerated the slice in a way that positively excluded the members the very run rendering it had just added — so it is dropped rather than re-typed: a fresh decomposition would be a third literal, and `population.files` carries the same fact derived. G21 refuses a figure here that the run did not derive. (Standing, not proven: the attempts were made and none succeeded. `UNFALSIFIED` here previously meant `not yet attempted`.) Ruling 5 asked for the control this artefact was unfalsified against: the generator refuses on each falsification class with the mutation committed and shown firing, a drifted per-row bucket assignment is caught naming the row and the buckets it crosses, and the artefact re-derives byte-identically from a second source path. That last is a CONSISTENCY pin, not a correctness claim (ruling 9, residual X6). Nothing here establishes that an axis verdict is RIGHT (X1), and nothing outside the declared population has been falsified at all — the tickets `population.outside_the_population.owners` names own that.

verdict_mapping.rule: SUCCESS -> :green. FAILURE -> :red. WARNING -> :green carrying warning: true.
verdict_mapping.warning_basis: PM-ratified D2, measured not chosen: WARNING is leg-dependent — the client-leg reducer fails it, `requirements_exit` and the server-leg reducer ignore it — and BOTH in-denominator WARNING checks are on the server leg, where the reducer that would disagree does not apply.
verdict_mapping.warning_live_data: EXERCISED on 1 cell(s) of this run's population — the mapping fires on real data and is no longer unit-tested only. WHAT THAT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that it is RIGHT. A mapping that labelled every non-red check `warning` would fire here exactly as readily, so `exercised` and `correct` are different claims and only the first is made by this count. The second is the business of `conformance/controls/crosswalk_falsification_controls.exs warning_mapping`, which requires the real WARNING cell to land where the mapping sends it AND requires it to move OUT when the OC verdict is mutated away from WARNING.
verdict_mapping.warning_residual: A future CLIENT-leg WARNING needs its own ruling. The mapping must not be extended to cover one silently.

what_this_is: The single matrix the ten buckets are PROJECTIONS of. C2 renders it, C3 falsifies it, D adjudicates its cells. It decides what no bucket MEANS.
